findings.consequence: The identity-capture branch calls process.communicate() without a timeout or signal. The PGID-mismatch branch also waits without a timeout. A hung child can exceed the 120-second outer bound, and cleanup/result evidence is not guaranteed. This violates the registered deadline and exact owned-process cleanup gate and can consume the one-shot marker without a usable calibration receipt.
findings.evidence: launch_once.py:181-193 claims the marker and spawns the child before identity capture. Lines 231-242 contain unbounded communicate() calls and no cleanup path on these errors.
findings.required_resolution: Handle every post-spawn failure under the outer deadline. Reap or terminate the still-owned direct child safely, use group signaling only after identity validation, and persist cleanup evidence. Re-freeze and re-review.
findings.title: Spawn identity failure bypasses bounded cleanup
findings.trigger: After Popen succeeds and the one-shot marker is claimed, ps identity capture returns a nonzero exit, malformed output, or a PGID different from the expected leader PID.

findings.consequence: The completed workload fails at the final measurement gate despite later valid positive MPS measurements. The calibration result is rejected and its one-shot marker is already consumed. The current negative control tests only an all-zero list; it misses mixed startup-zero/positive data.
findings.evidence: probe.py:195-219 starts the sampler, waits for its first complete sample, then loads best204 on MPS. Pinned R6 worker.py:569-573 queries current-process MPS driver allocation. probe.py:114-118 rejects every zero. test_calibration_cpu.py:118-137 covers all-zero but not mixed values.
findings.required_resolution: Keep every sample present, numeric, finite, and nonnegative; require positive measured allocation during the representative MPS workload (or define an explicit post-load acceptance window). Add a mixed startup-zero/positive predicate control. Re-freeze and re-review.
findings.title: MPS gate rejects any zero sample, including startup
findings.trigger: The sampler starts and writes its first sample before best204 is loaded onto MPS. If that valid startup query reports zero, while later samples report positive allocation, validation still runs all(value > 0 for value in mps_samples).
